title: delegation_limit has no owner in the P7 rows, and three sources name three different homes for the level
source: Context pack P7 ownership rows (6 tables); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07; Architecture v5 slide 13 (P7 to P4 = R); legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 4 and 12; FSD P7 A2.24
description: The level this story must read is a row of the delegation of authority table. The P7 ownership rows list approval, decision_log_entry, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case, so the table is not P7's and must be read through a contract. Which contract is not settled: the legacy story calls the in-process DelegationQuery of its own module, DP-07 sends reference data to the rwb-case contract, and the connection matrix gives P7 exactly one REST cell, to rwb-access (P4). The story follows the matrix and reads from P4, and the disagreement is recorded here so that the pattern table and the Ownership Map are corrected together.
evidence: Legacy section 4 step 4 reads 'reads the required level for the plan from the P7 DelegationQuery'; DP-07 reads 'Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case'; Architecture v5 slide 13 gives P7 a single R cell in the P4 column and leaves the P3 column empty; the context pack lists no delegation table among the six P7 tables.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the Ownership Map owner
proposed: Rule delegation_limit to rwb-access, publish the level read there with its fake, and correct the DP-07 row of the pattern table in its next version; the level, the delegation row id and the version stay on the approval row and on the D5 entry, and no copy of the table is made.

title: The delegation read of rwb-access has no named path, request, answer or message text
source: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 12 (DelegationQuery); FSD P7 A2.24 AC-ALT-P7-024-01 and AC-EXC-P7-024-04; Template and Rules R4 naming rules; TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A
description: The story needs the level, the delegation row id and the version in force for a decision code, a regulation item, a product group, an amount and a date, in one hop with a 2 s budget. The only source facts are the legacy Java signature without a date, the FSD lookup example that returns level L6 with the row id of item 2.1.1 at L6 and version DOA-2026.11 on 15 December 2026, and the NOT_COVERED answer with MSG-P7-010 in the FSD exception flow. No source gives the resource path under the rwb-access base, the query parameters, the body, the error codes, the text of MSG-P7-010, MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P4-003, or whether the lookup takes a date.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A lists the eight P7 endpoints and no delegation read; the Ownership Map P7 rows carry the operation only as a consumed dependency; FSD P7 A2.24 AC-EXC-P7-024-04 names NOT_COVERED and MSG-P7-010 with no schema.
proposed: Add the read to the rwb-access contract and to its row of the API Specification as GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits with decisionCode, regulationItem, productGroup, amount and asOfDate, answering level, delegationLimitId, limitVersion or NOT_COVERED, and publish the text of MSG-P7-010, MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P4-003 in the next message catalogue.

title: The field set of a D5 credit entry and the format of the NLEADS reference are not specified
source: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to 031); legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 11 and 12; FSD P7 A2.3 and A2.4
description: The entry must hold the level applied, the level the delegation required, the delegation row id and version, the NLEADS reference and the result date. TSD P7 T3.1 gives one approval_level column, one rule_version and the free jsonb fields recommendation, actions and outcome, so the required level and its version have no field of their own, the origin of inputs_ref is not stated, and the legacy story marks the NLEADS reference as 'format assumed until SCB IT confirms'. The story therefore writes the level applied in approval_level and the rest in actions, and the exact keys, the origin of the inputs snapshot and the 1 to 30 characters of the reference rest on the assumption.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists actions as free jsonb; legacy section 12 reads 'nleadsRef (1 to 30 letters, digits and dashes; format assumed until SCB IT confirms, DL12)'; no source lists the keys of actions for decision code D5.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the ledger owner
proposed: Fix the D5 key set of actions in the decision-record schema document as requiredLevel, delegationLimitId, limitVersion, nleadsRef and resultDate, take inputs_ref from the pack read reference, and confirm the NLEADS reference pattern with SCB IT before the wave 2 test cycle.

title: The legacy story requires the Treatment and offer right while the endpoint of this service declares the Decision log right
source: Legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 10 and 12; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P7-003, API-P7-005); FSD P7 A2.24; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08
description: The legacy operation requires 'Treatment and offer, U' and refuses a role without it with MSG-P4-002. The same action in the target is the approve and refuse operation of rwb-decision, whose TSD declaration is 'Decision log, right A, scope applied'. One caller therefore needs two rights in two capability areas, or one of the two declarations is wrong, and no source decides which. The story follows the declaration of the service that owns the operation, keeps the legacy MSG-P4-002 behaviour, and records the difference.
evidence: Legacy section 12 heads the credit-result operation 'Treatment and offer, U'; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 gives API-P7-003 and API-P7-005 'Decision log, right A, scope applied'; the RBAC matrix of T6.1 gives every role R on the Decision log and no A row at all.
owner_role: P4 access owner and the P7 solution architect
proposed: Declare Decision log right A on the two recording operations as the TSD does, add the A rows to the RBAC matrix for the roles that record a result, and keep the Treatment and offer right U on the pack endpoint of rwb-integration so that the officer still needs both to complete the flow.

title: How a D5 credit approval is identified, and whether a result is an approve or a dedicated credit-result action, is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 4 and 12 (credit-result operation); Ownership Map v1 P7 provided operations; TSD P7 v2 API-P7-003 and API-P7-005
description: The legacy story records a credit result through POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result with APPROVED or REFUSED. The Ownership Map carries no such operation on P7; the nearest owned operations are approve and refuse on an approval, and the approval row is created by the routing slice. Two facts are therefore unsettled: which approval a credit result addresses, expressed as the source_type and source_ref of the D5 row for a treatment, and how the two NLEADS results map onto the approval statuses APPROVED and REFUSED. The story maps APPROVED to approve and REFUSED to refuse and keeps one result per approval.
evidence: Legacy section 12 names POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result; the P7 ownership rows list GET and POST operations on /approvals/{approvalId} only; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives approval.source_type and source_ref with no value list.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the routing story owner
proposed: Fix source_type CREDIT_APPROVAL and source_ref as the treatment id for a D5 row in the data dictionary, and state in the Service Contract Catalog that a credit result is recorded through approve or refuse on that row.

title: The event name that carries the D5 record on the service topic is not stated
source: Architecture v5 slide 13 (rwb-reporting subscribes to P7 events); TSD P7 v2 T5.3; Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-14; Ownership Map v1 P7 events EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30
description: The event of a decision record is one fact on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and the matrix gives rwb-reporting an event subscription to P7. P7 owns three event identifiers and the TSD names two published events, DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested, without saying which of them travels on rwb.decision.events.v1 or in which payload. The story names the fact rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 on both topics by the naming rule and leaves the identifier mapping open.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T5.3 lists DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested as Published with no topic; the Ownership Map gives EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 with no names; slide 13 gives the P9 row an E in the P7 column.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the event catalogue owner
proposed: Publish rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision.events.v1 as well as on the shared ledger topic, keyed by case id with IDs, codes, levels and dates only, and map it to the free identifier of EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog.

title: The platform contracts the DP table adds are not in the metadata build row, and one provided operation has no story
source: Template and Rules R5.5 (DP-03, DP-07, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.7; context pack P7 ownership rows (19 provided operations)
description: Four of the seven patterns applied here carry an H platform contract of the DP table, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, while the work package gives H, C, I and X as empty and the story is Day 1 in lane L-P7-T; the two statements are both kept and the difference is recorded. In the same way the service provides 19 operations of which this story provides five, and GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation has no story among the P7 set that claims it.
evidence: The DP table names the four platform contracts against DP-03, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19; the work package line for this story lists H, C, I and X as empty arrays; the Ownership Map lists 19 P7 provided operations and the P7 service story set names no owner for the recommendation read.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the story-catalogue owner
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the work package gives them, treat the four platform contracts as published before Day 1 work starts, and give the recommendation read to the P7 story that serves the decision screen in the next version of the Service Story Catalog.
